items.prose: A microscopic void in the borosilicate glass dielectric tube caused localized electric arcing under 12.5 kV. The intense plasma discharge punctured the glass wall, short-circuiting the power supply and reducing generator ozone output by half.

Scale buildup inside the downstream booster pump impeller dropped differential pressure across the 316-stainless venturi educator. Without adequate pressure drop, vacuum suction failed, and ozone gas bubbles backed up into the safety check valve.

Dispersing ozone gas through microporous ceramic diffusers at the base of a six-meter column established counter-current flow against descending water. The system achieved a CT value of 1.6 mg·min/L, inactivating 99.99% of enteric viruses.

Residual ozone off-gas venting from the contact chamber passed through a heated granular manganese dioxide catalyst bed. The catalytic reaction converted 99.9% of residual O3 back into breathable oxygen, keeping room air below the 0.1 ppm exposure limit.

Saturated molecular sieve desiccant allowed feed air dew point to rise from -60°C to -15°C. In the corona gap, atmospheric moisture reacted with nitrogen oxides to synthesize nitric acid vapor, corroding the aluminum discharge electrodes into white crumbly powder.

Ozonating brackish groundwater containing 0.3 mg/L bromide ions formed carcinogenic bromate (BrO3-) at 28 ppb. Dosing dilute sulfuric acid to suppress influent pH from 8.2 down to 6.5 shifted oxidation kinetics, keeping bromate below the 10 ppb safety threshold.

An erroneous maintenance replacement installed nitrile (Buna-N) flange gaskets on the concentrated ozone piping. Within ten days, ozone cleaved the polymer double bonds, cracking the gaskets into brittle crumbs; all seals were replaced with PTFE-encapsulated Viton.

Low-dose pre-ozonation (0.8 mg/L) oxidized dissolved fulvic and humic acids chelating radioactive heavy metal ions. The micro-flocculation effect aggregated microscopic colloids into settleable flocs, improving downstream sand filter retention by 40%.
